titleStmt.title: Giuseppe riconosciuto, dramma sacro per musica

work.title: Giuseppe riconosciuto, dramma sacro per musica
Joseph, som giver sig tilkiende for sine Brødre. Et musikalsk Stykke

history.p: The present large-scale dramatic cantata or oratorio, of which only the text book has survived, was performed on three consecutive Sundays, 1, 8 and 15 October 1769, at the hall of The Musical Society. It is not clear whether the whole cantata was performed on each occasion, or whether the work was divided into three sections though that would most likely have meant a somewhat artificial division of the cantata. The concert was advertised in the newspaper, Kiøbenhavns Adresse-Contoirs Efterretninger, throughout the period, and tickets could be bought by contacting Scheibe at his home address between 8 and 12 o'clock in the morning. It is one of the few works to which Scheibe employed an Italian text; however, as Scheibe clearly states in his introduction to his opera 'Thusnelde' (1749; SchW B1:002), he thought highly of Metastasio’s poetical and dramatic works. It therefore seems quite natural that he chose his ‘Giuseppe riconosciuto’ of 1733. The popular text had already been used by Johann Adolph Hasse in 1741, whose works Scheibe greatly admired, as well as by the Kapellmeister Paolo Scalabrini seven years before his arrival at the Danish court.

annot.p: 'NB. NB. Musikens Velyndere og Liebhabere bekiendtgiøres, at den 1ste, 8de og 15de October næstkommende, bliver om Eftermiddagen præcise Kl. 5. paa Bryggeres Laugshuus-Sahl, opført et stort Drammatisk Synge-Stykke under Titul: G[iu]seppe riconosciuto, Dramma sacro per Musica, eller Joseph, som giver sig tilkiende for sine Brødre: Et Synge-Stykke af den hellige Skrift. Poesien er af den berømte Abbed Metasta[s]io, og den dertil nye componerede Musik af Capellmester Scheibe. Entreen koster pro Persona 1 Rdlr., hvorfor tillige gratis bekommes den trykte Italienske Text vedsatte Hr. Soelbergs Danske Oversettelse. Liebhaberne kan og bekomme Billets til Entre pro Persona for alle 3de Gange, eller og hvorpaa en Aften 3 Personer kan indgaae, Stykket 2 Rdlr. men hvorimod de den trykte Text betaler med 1 Mk. Danske. Billetterne kan fra i Dag af bekommes alle Formiddage fra Kl. 8 til 12 hos Capellmester Scheibe, boende i Reverentz-Gaden, imellem Hr. Cammer-Raad Post og Tracteuren Monsr. Marechall.'

incipText.p: Nè degl Ebrei germani in Mensi ancora nessuno ritorno?
Er ingen af de Jødiske Brødre endnu komne tilbage til Memphis?
Og dette er nok til at foruroelige dig?
Consorte, è a me permesso sperar grazia da te?
Min Mand! er mig tilladt at vente en Naade af dig?
Dersom du ei vil at han maa blive frie
Naar man kuns kaster sine Øjne
Vien Simeone. Oh se pensar potesse
Der kommer Simeon. O dersom han kunde tænke
Jeg vilde, for at trøste ham
Defendi il popol tuo, gran Dio d'Abramo!
Du store Abrahams Gud! Beskierm dit Folk!
Jeg veed, at den taber Æren
Tu che dell' alme nostre eterna Verità, vedi gli arcani
Du, evige Sandhed, som seer vores Sieles Hemmeligheder
Jeg vil være som en kierlig Moder
Ak min Mand, du har sagt sandt
Jeg seer mig i en forfærdelig mørk og fæl Skov
No, no tanto rigore tolga il ciel ch'io dimostri
Nei, Himlen forbyde at jeg skulde vise saa stor Strænghed
Holder Stand, I mine Sinds Lidelser
Folle chi oppone i suoi a' consigli di Dio
Det er en Daare som opsetter sine Raad imod Guds Raad

physDesc.physMedium: In 8o; front flyleaf, title page (sig. [A1r]; p. [1]), list of characters and information on author and composer in Italian (sig. [A1v]; p. [2]), the same in Danish (sig. [A2r]; p. [3]), text with the original Italian on verso and with Danish translation on recto (pp. [4]–55), blank page, end flyleaf; in all 55 pages.
In contemporary limp binding with dark brown marbled covers, label with the initials 'B.J.H' and signature added in ink pasted on spine; paper of a dense and coarse quality.
In modern binding; paper of an inferior quality with no visible watermarks or countermarks.
